title: Purpose, first action and success up front
statement: Before work begins, show the learner its purpose, the first action and what success will look like, in words the learner can read, not only in review documents.
detail: The golden student-course standard asks of every lesson whether the intended outcome is observable and clear to the learner. It accepts a lesson when one declared operation, a learner-readable purpose, the first action and the success evidence are visible before work begins, and counts as failures a generic skill label, several competing goals, a hidden first action and success described only to the people reviewing it. Its claim boundary adds that plain language must keep the true cognitive demand. In one course's preflight, the simulated student's first probe asks for the same before the first action: what to do, what information matters and what success will look like.
